subject: Re: VPC packaging — oncall pass-through, carryforward credits & burst pricing
messages:
From: Sanaa Malik <sanaa@bluehavenhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on private deployment pricing and oncall charge-through

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the updated draft term sheet — Bluehaven's procurement and engineering teams reviewed it and we have a handful of clarifying questions before we start routing for internal approval. Attaching the RFP Qs PDF with line references. High level items:  

- Platform fee amortization: can this be invoiced monthly (vs upfront) for a 12‑month commitment?
- Carryforward credits: if our consumption is below committed capacity, can unused committed tokens be carried forward? If so, for how long and are there limits?
- Emergency burst pricing: your note references a burst uplift but doesn’t show pricing mechanics (GPU‑hour uplift vs per‑token uplift).
- SRE/oncall pass‑through: the RFP is asking whether Redwood will bill for SRE oncall time as a separate line item or embed it in the platform fee. How have you structured this for similar customers?

We'd like to keep commercial discussions tight — would appreciate a brief written response to the above plus any suggested invoice cadence. If needed we can set a 30‑minute call.

Best,
Sanaa Malik
Head of Procurement, Bluehaven Health

Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment pricing and oncall charge-through

Hi Sanaa — thanks for the clear list. Below are our proposals and clarifications; happy to hop on a call if you'd rather walk these items through.

1) Platform fee amortization
   - We can amortize the platform fee monthly across the 12‑month term instead of billing it upfront. We'll provide a quarterly statement that shows the amortization schedule and any prorations for the initial invoice period.

2) Carryforward credits (unused committed capacity)
   - Standard: up to 6 months carryforward of committed capacity, capped at 100% of a single month's committed volume (i.e., you cannot accumulate beyond one month’s equivalent in any carryforward window).
   - Flex option (one‑time): if Bluehaven increases commit during the term by >=25%, we can extend carryforward to 9 months for the remaining term.

3) Emergency burst pricing
   - Two options we commonly offer:
     a) GPU‑hour uplift: urgent GPU bursts billed at 1.7x standard GPU‑hour rate (best for short, high‑sustained loads).
     b) Per‑token uplift: 1.5x per‑token rate for bursted requests routed to reserved but scaled capacity.
   - We can include an automatic fallback to the cheaper of the two depending on workload profile.

4) SRE / oncall pass‑through
   - Typical approach: base SRE coverage is included in the platform fee for standard SLAs (uptime and monitoring). Oncall incident handling beyond SLA response windows is billed separately as a pass‑through (time & materials) or covered by a retainer.
   - Proposal for Bluehaven: optional monthly oncall retainer ($8,500/month) that covers up to two escalations/month; additional incidents billed at a per‑incident rate ($1,200/incident) with pre‑agreed severity definitions. This keeps invoices predictable for routine support while allowing on‑demand assistance for major incidents.

Next steps: I've attached our current term sheet (Redwood_Private_TermSheet_v3.pdf). I'd propose a short call with Mateo to align on the oncall boundaries and with Vanessa to capture your preferred invoice cadence and PO timing. Are you available tomorrow afternoon?

Regards,
Soojin Lee

Hi Sanaa — quick technical follow up from the infra/ops side to complement Soojin's commercial framing.

- Oncall pass‑through scope: when we bill incidents as pass‑through we only include Redwood‑delivered time (no third‑party contractor time). We'll record incident start/end and provide a short incident summary line item for the invoice.
- Response SLAs: standard target is 30‑minute response for Sev‑1, 2‑hour for Sev‑2. Our retainer includes guaranteed escalation staffing for Sev‑1 during business hours and an agreed after‑hours rota for critical support.
- Burst control knobs: to keep emergency costs reasonable we can apply dynamic caps (e.g., max 48 GPU‑hours per incident before manual approval) and pre‑approved scaling windows.
- Cost mitigation: recommend enabling our prefix/KV cache and increasing batching thresholds during predictable nightly jobs — customers have seen a ~30% effective token cost reduction.

I've sketched a simple pricing model for oncall scenarios in the attached spreadsheet (SRE_Pricing_Sketch.xlsx). If Bluehaven has expected monthly incident counts, I can quickly model the expected monthly cost under the retainer vs T&M.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin/Mateo, this is helpful. A few clarifying asks before we move to PO intent:  

- Invoice cadence: procurement prefers quarterly invoicing where possible. Will Redwood accept quarterly invoices tied to the amortization schedule (i.e., aggregated monthly amortized amounts invoiced quarterly)?
- Carryforward window: your standard 6 months is acceptable as a starting point. Bluehaven would like a contractual option to extend carryforward to 12 months if we commit to a 20% higher annual volume at renewal. Is Redwood open to that uplift for renewal commitments?
- Discount tiers: please provide the discount thresholds for 12‑month volume bands (we're considering a firm +25% and +50% uplift scenarios).
- DocuSign: please send the final term sheet for signature; we aim to get internal approvals by 2 March.

If we can close these points, procurement will issue a non‑binding PO intent this week.

Thanks,
Bluehaven Procurement

Hi — quick responses and a compromise that should align with your approval timelines.

- Invoice cadence: yes, we can invoice quarterly. We'll aggregate the monthly amortized platform fee and include monthly usage detail as a supplemental schedule.
- Carryforward window: we can agree to a renewal clause that expands carryforward up to 12 months, conditional on Bluehaven committing to >=20% uplift at renewal. For the current term we'll keep the 6‑month standard and include a one‑time option to extend to 9 months mid‑term if you notify us within 60 days of signing and increase commit by >=25%.
- Discount tiers (annualized committed volume):
   - Tier A (base): up to committed volume — list pricing
   - Tier B (+25% commit): 8% discount on token rate and 5% off platform fee
   - Tier C (+50% commit): 14% discount on token rate and 10% off platform fee

- DocuSign: attaching the updated term sheet and DocuSign link, please use the following for signature: https://docusign.com/00ABC123 . We'll mark the term sheet with the quarterly invoicing and the renewal carryforward clause.

Next steps: Vanessa will send a short commercial summary and the final DocuSign envelope by EOD. If you want, we can set a 20‑minute call Monday to walk procurement through the invoice example.

Appreciate the speedy collaboration — looking forward to closing this.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
